candidates.source_name: Twisto payments a.s. – Pro média (press release archive)
candidates.why_relevant: Twisto is the largest Czech-origin BNPL/wallet provider (CZ, PL, RO) and now part of the Turkish fintech group Param. Its media page carries a dense, dated archive of 100+ press releases running from 2013 to at least Jan 2026, covering market entries (e.g. Bulgaria, Dec 2025), merchant-portfolio expansion, consumer-payment surveys and Black Friday/seasonal spending data. This is the single richest continuously-published CZ BNPL press stream and directly feeds A1 topics (press releases, disclosures). A press kit (photos, org info) is linked via Google Drive and the media contact is pr@twisto.cz.
candidates.legal_status: publicly published corporate communications; standard copyright applies
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled HTML crawl of the listing page with pagination follow-through into individual release pages; extract title, date, body. Check for an RSS/JSON feed first. Re-crawl weekly.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of twisto.cz homepage, then navigation snowball into the press section

candidates.source_name: Twisto – Seznam e-shopů (partner merchant directory)
candidates.why_relevant: A categorised, browsable directory of merchants that accept Twisto (fashion, health & beauty, auto-moto, electronics, food & drink, etc.), with 'Nejpopulárnější / Nejnovější / Doporučujeme' sections and a 'Zobrazit všechny e-shopy' full listing. Observed names include Allegro.cz, Planeo.cz, Smarty.cz, Kiwi.com, Reserved.com, Datart.cz, Mode.cz. Diffing this list over time is a direct, structured read on which Czech merchants are adopting or dropping BNPL at checkout — intelligence that neither bank IR nor gateway marketing publishes.
candidates.legal_status: public marketing directory; treat as factual listing, avoid wholesale republication
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of the full listing (follow the 'all e-shops' link and category filters); store merchant name + category + first/last seen date to build an adoption time series.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from twisto.cz/mam-eshop/ merchant landing page

candidates.source_name: Twisto Developer Documentation (docs.twisto.cz)
candidates.why_relevant: Technical documentation exposing exactly how Twisto plugs into Czech checkouts: a Merchant API (with a 'create a checkout' guide), promotional Widgets, and a dedicated PSP API for payment service providers, plus two explicitly deprecated paths (Eshop-API/Twisto.js, described as CZ-market-only, and the Twisto Universal API for gateways). Deprecation notices and PSP-facing endpoints are a rare, dateable signal of checkout-technology direction and of which gateways Twisto expects to ride on. Czech-language variant at /cs.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly snapshot of the docs tree (or git-style diff of rendered pages) to detect new/deprecated endpoints and newly named gateway partners.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from twisto.cz/mam-eshop/

candidates.source_name: Twisto – Podmínky pro obchodníky a Registrace ČNB (merchant T&Cs and licence disclosures)
candidates.why_relevant: Twisto's legal hub carries merchant terms (podmínky pro obchodníky), pre-contractual information, the client guide, complaint rules, whistleblowing policy and — notably — a dedicated page on its ČNB registration. Merchant T&Cs are the place where fee structures, settlement terms and integration obligations become documented rather than marketed; the ČNB-registration page anchors the regulated-entity identity (Twisto payments a.s., licensed payment institution, Principal Member of Mastercard and Visa Europe, PCI DSS Level 1).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Version-tracked fetch of each terms page (semi-annual), diffing for fee/scope changes; archive PDFs where offered.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of twisto.cz homepage footer

candidates.source_name: Param (Param Financial Technologies, TR) – group site and press section, owner of Twisto
candidates.why_relevant: Twisto's own 'O nás' page states 'Dnes je Twisto součástí fintechu Param'; Param's group-companies section lists Twisto explicitly ('Twisto - Avrupa'da BNPL ile Kredili Alışveriş') and links to twisto.cz. Ownership moved out of the Australian Zip Co orbit into a Turkish group, which changes where group-level financial and strategic disclosure about the Czech BNPL business will appear. Worth tracking as the parent-level channel even though it is Turkish-language and not an EU-listed issuer.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency (monthly) crawl of the /basin press listing with machine translation TR->EN; filter for 'Twisto', 'Çekya', 'Avrupa'.
candidates.discovered_via_method: ownership snowball from twisto.cz/o-nas/ then direct fetch of param.com.tr

candidates.source_name: Skip Pay (ČSOB) – Tiskové zprávy / Pro novináře
candidates.why_relevant: Skip Pay (formerly MallPay, IČO 07093331, part of ČSOB/KBC) is the flagship bank-owned Czech deferred-payment arm. Its press stream mixes consumer-advice pieces with genuinely quantitative disclosures — e.g. the 05.02.2026 release stating 99% of Skip Pay customers repay on time and framing deferred payment as cash-flow optimisation. The 'Pro novináře' page adds a named spokesperson (František Brož, pr@skippay.cz) plus downloadable logo, illustrative photo and infographic ZIP bundles.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly crawl of /tiskove-zpravy listing plus individual release pages; separately snapshot the infographic ZIP from /pro-novinare as it periodically carries hard numbers not present in the text.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of skippay.cz then navigation snowball

candidates.source_name: Skip Pay Developer Portal (developers.skippay.eu)
candidates.why_relevant: The most explicit map found of Czech BNPL checkout plumbing. The /pro-vyvojare page and the developer portal together enumerate native plugins (Shoptet — two versions, WooCommerce, PrestaShop, OpenCart, Drupal Commerce, Virtuemart, Magento, TheShop), payment-gateway routes (ČSOB Payment Gateway, Comgate, TrustPay, GoPay) and Czech SaaS e-shop platforms (ITStudio, Shopty, eBrana, Fastcentrik, Retailys, JZShop, Binargon). That gateway + SaaS-platform list is a direct read on the Czech e-commerce technology stack around deferred payment.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly snapshot of the docs tree and the /pro-vyvojare integration matrix; extract the plugin/gateway/SaaS lists into a structured table and diff between runs.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from skippay.cz navigation into /pro-vyvojare, then to the external developer domain

candidates.source_name: Skip Pay – Dokumenty (terms, pricing, information memorandum)
candidates.why_relevant: Consolidated legal/document hub for the ČSOB-owned deferred-payment arm: terms, privacy and pricing documents, plus a separate information memorandum and an accessibility statement PDF. Pricing/terms documents are where BNPL economics (late fees, instalment charges, merchant obligations) are stated in binding form rather than in marketing copy.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Semi-annual fetch with PDF archiving and text diffing to catch fee/term changes.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of skippay.cz footer navigation

candidates.source_name: Home Credit a.s. (CZ) – Tiskové zprávy
candidates.why_relevant: Home Credit a.s. (IČO 269 78 636, Nové sady 996/25, Brno; PPF group) is the incumbent Czech point-of-sale consumer-credit house and is authorised by ČNB both as a payment institution and as a non-bank consumer-credit provider. Its press stream is active and substantive: product launches (12.08.2026, a purpose loan for entrepreneurs up to CZK 2m), strategic exits (19.05.2026, ending short-term lending — 'Mise Kamali byla splněna'), and recurring proprietary household-finance surveys (29.07.2026, 20.07.2026, 06.05.2026). Product-exit announcements of this kind are exactly the sort of disclosure that reframes the consumer-credit competitive map.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly crawl of the listing plus release detail pages; tag releases by type (product / survey / corporate) since surveys and product changes need different downstream handling.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of homecredit.cz, then snowball via /o-nas

candidates.source_name: Home Credit Group – Financial Disclosures and News & Media
candidates.why_relevant: Group-level channel for the Home Credit franchise, carrying a 'Financial Disclosures' section plus a News & Media centre and a series of sustainability/ESG reports (2020 ESG, 2021 and 2022 sustainability reports served as PDFs from /wp-content/uploads/). Group disclosures are where consolidated consumer-finance metrics and strategic repositioning appear; the Czech entity is not separately paged on the group site, so CZ-specific figures must be triangulated from group filings plus the Czech Sbírka listin.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly crawl of /financial-disclosures/ and /news-media/; harvest linked PDFs (pattern /wp-content/uploads/YYYY/MM/*.pdf) and index by report year.
candidates.discovered_via_method: parent-group snowball from homecredit.cz

candidates.source_name: PPF Group – Financial results, reports and press releases (owner of Home Credit and Air Bank/Zonky)
candidates.why_relevant: PPF is the ultimate owner of both Home Credit a.s. and Air Bank a.s. (which now operates Zonky), so its consolidated reporting and press releases are the only place where these two Czech consumer-credit franchises are discussed in one financial frame. Observed a dated group press release on 2025 performance ('In 2025 PPF confirmed the strong performance of its key business lines...', published 20 May 2026) alongside a reports-and-documents hub carrying the PPF 2025 report.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly crawl of the financial-reports and reports-and-documents pages plus the press-release index; filter releases for 'Home Credit', 'Air Bank', 'Zonky', 'consumer finance'. Czech-language mirror exists under /cs.
candidates.discovered_via_method: ownership snowball from homecredit.cz and zonky.cz footer ('člen skupiny PPF')

candidates.source_name: ESSOX s.r.o. – Tiskové zprávy
candidates.why_relevant: ESSOX (F. A. Gerstnera 52, České Budějovice; Komerční banka / Société Générale group) is the bank-owned instalment-finance arm and a Shoptet checkout provider ('ESSOX Payments'). Its press archive is paginated across roughly six pages and carries genuinely quantitative and commercially revealing items: renewal of captive brand financing for Kia (06.02.2024) and for Peugeot/Citroën/DS (01.02.2024), +60% growth in e-bike financing (12.12.2023), 30-year anniversary with two million contracts (07.11.2023), 840 new motorcycles financed in H1 (02.08.2023), and 'Obliba Rozložené platby roste' (01.09.2022) on its split-payment product. It also publishes e-commerce behavioural research (30.11.2022, on the price threshold at which shoppers abandon an e-shop for a physical store).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl all listing pages (observed pagination 1-6) then each release; monthly re-crawl. Also pull /pro-obchodni-partnery and /dokumenty-ke-stazeni for merchant-facing terms.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of essox.cz then navigation snowball into the press archive

candidates.source_name: COFIDIS a.s. (CZ) – corporate site, O nás / Partnerská zóna / Nákup na splátky
candidates.why_relevant: Cofidis a.s. is the Czech arm of the French COFIDIS group (parent: COFIDIS, société anonyme, Villeneuve d'Ascq, ID 325 307 106 RCS Lille) and is a ČLFA member. Its site structure exposes an 'O nás' area with news, corporate responsibility and awards, a 'Nákup na splátky' section covering e-shops, physical stores and auto loans, downloadable documents and GDPR/consumer-rights pages, plus a separate Partnerská zóna for merchants. It publishes representative APRC examples (e.g. CZK 200,000 loan, monthly instalment CZK 5,179, RPSN 11.68, total payable CZK 248,592) and cites the Index odpovědného úvěrování and Zlatá koruna awards. Cofidis also ships two distinct Shoptet checkout products (Cofidis iPlatba and Cofidis Pay Na splátky).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Render-capable crawl (the nav appears to be JS-assembled; several guessed press paths 404'd) starting from the homepage, following 'O nás' -> novinky and 'Nákup na splátky'; capture RPSN representative examples as a pricing time series.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of cofidis.cz homepage; press-path guesses returned 404 so exact news URL is unresolved
candidates.observed_blocker: Guessed news paths /tiskove-zpravy, /o-nas, /o-nas.html and /cs/o-nas/novinky.html all returned HTTP 404; homepage nav references 'novinky' but the resolved path was not determined.

candidates.source_name: PlatímPak (Raiffeisenbank) – bank-owned BNPL: media page, merchant pages and e-shop directory
candidates.why_relevant: PlatímPak is Raiffeisenbank's own deferred-payment brand — a squarely on-cell 'bank-owned deferred-payment arm' that was not in the seed list. Product terms are disclosed on-site: purchases up to CZK 25,000, 30 days interest-free, or instalments, provided by a bank under ČNB supervision. Critically it publishes a merchant directory (/seznam-eshopu) and a merchant-acquisition page (/pro-eshopy), plus a media page with brand manual, two logo versions and a named spokesperson (PhDr. Tereza Kaiseršotová). Privacy handling is routed to rb.cz, confirming the Raiffeisenbank legal spine.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of /seznam-eshopu (merchant adoption time series) and /dulezite-dokumenty (terms diffs); note that /pro-media hosts contacts and brand assets only, so actual releases must be picked up from Raiffeisenbank's own media centre.
candidates.discovered_via_method: discovered via the Shoptet payments addon catalogue, then direct fetch of platimpak.cz

candidates.source_name: Shoptet Doplňky – Platby category (BNPL/instalment addon catalogue)
candidates.why_relevant: The single best pointer source found for this cell. Shoptet is the dominant Czech e-shop SaaS platform and its addon marketplace (403 addons at time of fetch) enumerates, in one place, every payment and deferred-payment provider competing for Czech checkouts: Shoptet Pay, Shoptet Boost (financing), PayPal, Cofidis iPlatba, GoPay+, Comgate, Lemonero (working capital), ThePay, Pays, HomeCredit, PlatímPak, Barion, ESSOX Payments, Skip Pay, Global Payments 2.0, Twisto Pay+, Cofidis Pay Na splátky, Inbank, Smable, Pluxee Flexi, Cashbot Pay, Skip Pay PREMIUM, PayU PREMIUM, Pluxee Gastro. It surfaced three actors absent from the seed brief (PlatímPak, Inbank, Cashbot Pay) and distinguishes standard vs PREMIUM tiers, which is itself a commercial signal.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of the /category/platby index and each addon detail page; extract provider name, tier, install/rating metadata if exposed, and first/last seen. Use as the actor-discovery feed that seeds deeper per-provider collection.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles reasoning that the dominant e-shop platform's addon store must reveal checkout-technology choices; direct fetch then category snowball

candidates.source_name: Inbank (AS Inbank, odštěpný závod CZ) – Czech site and group investor portal
candidates.why_relevant: Estonian licensed bank operating in CZ through a branch (AS Inbank, odštěpný závod; Lazarská 13/8, Praha 2) and distributing point-of-sale instalment financing via Shoptet. It combines a Czech-language retail/merchant site (/pro-obchodni-partnery, /cenik, an annual-percentage-rates PDF) with a genuine group investor portal at inbank.eu/investors — meaning, unlike most CZ BNPL players, audited group financials are published on a regular cadence and can be read against the Czech branch's local activity.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly crawl of inbank.eu/investors for reports/presentations; separately monitor inbank.cz/pro-obchodni-partnery and the APRC PDF for CZ pricing and merchant-programme changes.
candidates.discovered_via_method: discovered via the Shoptet payments addon catalogue, then direct fetch of inbank.cz

candidates.source_name: Zonky (Air Bank a.s.) and Air Bank – Rozložení platby, Pro novináře
candidates.why_relevant: Zonky has been absorbed into Air Bank: the site footer reads '© 2026 Air Bank a.s., člen skupiny PPF, poskytovatel služby Zonky', so Zonky is now a service of the bank rather than a standalone P2P platform. This matters for the cell because it means Zonky-specific disclosure has migrated to Air Bank and PPF channels. Air Bank itself operates a deferred/split-payment product (/rozlozeni-platby/) and a Zonky Rentier investment product, and maintains a journalist page and a news feed. Zonky retains /o-zonky/, /dokumenty/, /cenik/ and an affiliate programme.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Track Air Bank's /novinky/ and /pro-novinare/ as the live press channel; snapshot zonky.cz/dokumenty/ and /cenik/ semi-annually for terms drift. Do not expect a standalone Zonky press room — none exists.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of zonky.cz, ownership snowball to airbank.cz

candidates.source_name: Cashbot / Cashbot Pay – Czech SME financing fintech
candidates.why_relevant: Czech alternative-financing fintech whose Cashbot Pay product is B2B deferred payment — 'Plaťte svým dodavatelům na třetiny a bez navýšení' (pay suppliers in three instalments at no extra cost) — and which is distributed through the Shoptet checkout catalogue. It extends the cell beyond consumer BNPL into merchant-side/B2B deferred payment, which is where several Czech providers are expanding. Site carries a press-coverage page, blog, case studies and references.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly crawl of /napsali-o-nas/ (press-coverage index, doubles as a media-source discovery feed), /blog/ and /cashbotpay/.
candidates.discovered_via_method: discovered via the Shoptet payments addon catalogue, then direct fetch of cashbot.cz

candidates.source_name: MONETA Money Bank – Vztahy s investory
candidates.why_relevant: MONETA is a Prague-listed bank whose franchise is heavily consumer-lending weighted (and whose MONETA Auto arm is a ČLFA member), making its mandatory disclosures the most granular regularly-audited window onto Czech consumer-credit volumes available in this cell. The IR site advertises annual reports, financial results and mandatory disclosures ('Výroční zprávy, hospodářské výsledky, povinně uveřejňované informace'), an IR calendar and a company-documents section. Whether it breaks out point-of-sale/deferred payment specifically was not established from the landing page.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Subscribe to the IR calendar (/ir-kalendar) and crawl /financni-vysledky and /dokumenty-spolecnosti quarterly; harvest PDFs and parse the consumer-lending segment tables.
candidates.discovered_via_method: actor-map reasoning about Czech bank-owned consumer-credit arms; direct fetch

candidates.source_name: Obchodní rejstřík / Sbírka listin – Czech Ministry of Justice public registers
candidates.why_relevant: The authoritative and legally mandated route to statutory annual reports and audited financial statements (výroční zprávy, účetní závěrky) for every entity in this cell — Twisto payments a.s., Skip Pay s.r.o. (IČO 07093331), Home Credit a.s. (IČO 269 78 636), ESSOX s.r.o., COFIDIS a.s., Zaplo Finance s.r.o. and the rest. Most of these companies publish no financial statements on their own websites, so the Sbírka listin is the only primary financial source. A new unified portal has launched (verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz, with basic and /rozsirene-vyhledavani advanced search) while or.justice.cz, esf.justice.cz and esm.justice.cz remain the official data sources; an open-data endpoint exists at dataor.justice.cz under Act No. 106/1999 Sb.
candidates.legal_status: official public register; open data provision under Act No. 106/1999 Sb.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Resolve each cell actor to its IČO once, then poll the Sbírka listin per IČO on a quarterly cadence for newly filed účetní závěrka / výroční zpráva PDFs. Prefer the dataor.justice.cz open-data feed for bulk register metadata; fall back to the or.justice.cz UI for document retrieval. Both the new portal and the open-data page rendered as near-empty shells to a plain HTTP fetch, so a headless-browser or the documented data endpoints will be needed.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles reasoning (who MUST publish) plus direct fetch of or.justice.cz, which surfaced the new msp.gov.cz portal and the dataor open-data endpoint
candidates.observed_blocker: Both verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz and dataor.justice.cz returned essentially empty content to a plain fetch (JS-rendered shells) — a hypothesis of client-side rendering, not evidence the services are down.

candidates.source_name: ČNB JERRS – Seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů (+ WS JERRS web services)
candidates.why_relevant: The regulator's own register of every licensed/registered financial-market entity, and therefore the definitive way to establish and monitor the licence status of each actor in this cell — non-bank consumer-credit providers (nebankovní poskytovatel spotřebitelského úvěru), payment institutions and e-money institutions. Home Credit a.s. states it is authorised in ČNB's register both as a payment institution and a non-bank consumer-credit provider; Twisto states it is a licensed payment institution under ČNB supervision. Machine access exists: 'WS JERRS' web services have provided selected entity information since 1 July 2019. Corrections contact: seznamy.subjektu@cnb.cz.
candidates.legal_status: official regulator register, published for public verification
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the WS JERRS web services rather than scraping the Oracle-style web UI: pull the full list of nebankovní poskytovatelé spotřebitelského úvěru and platební instituce monthly, diff for new licences, withdrawals and changes of control. This doubles as a systematic actor-discovery feed for the whole cell.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles reasoning (who regulates) plus direct fetch of the ČNB seznamy page, then following the 302 redirect to the JERRS application

candidates.source_name: ČLFA – Česká leasingová a finanční asociace (statistics, press, member list)
candidates.why_relevant: Trade association for Czech non-bank finance, explicitly covering 'spotřebitelské úvěry a spotřebitelský leasing' and stating it represents 14 licensed consumer-credit providers. It publishes market statistics, a market-information section, its own annual reports and a press-release stream — the closest thing to sector-level volume data for non-bank consumer credit. Its verified member list is also an actor map for this cell: COFIDIS a.s., ESSOX s.r.o., Home Credit a.s., Twisto Payments a.s., Zaplo Finance s.r.o. and MONETA Auto s.r.o. all appear, confirming Twisto's positioning inside the regulated non-bank finance establishment rather than outside it. Contact: clfa@clfa.cz, Italská 2584/69, Praha 2.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly crawl of /statistiky and /statistiky/informace-o-trhu for released datasets, /pro-media/tiskove-zpravy for commentary, and re-fetch the member list semi-annually as an actor-map refresh.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles reasoning (who aggregates) plus direct fetch, then snowball into the member list

candidates.source_name: SOLUS – zájmové sdružení právnických osob (credit registry: member list and debt statistics)
candidates.why_relevant: SOLUS operates Czech client-information registries (registers of individuals, entrepreneurs, creditworthiness and third parties). Two uses for this cell. First, its member list is an actor-discovery feed that surfaced consumer-credit players outside the seed brief: ESSOX s.r.o., Creditstar Czech s.r.o., CreditPortal a.s., PROFI CREDIT Czech a.s., AvaFin Czech s.r.o., Simfina a.s. Second, its aktuality stream publishes hard arrears statistics — e.g. a release dated 30 April 2026 reporting that consumers owe SOLUS members CZK 34.6bn in overdue debt — which is the sector-level credit-quality series against which individual BNPL providers' 'our customers repay on time' claims can be tested.
candidates.legal_status: public association publications; the registries themselves are not public
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of /aktuality/ to capture the recurring arrears statistics releases; semi-annual re-fetch of /clenske-spolecnosti/ as an actor-map refresh. Registry contents themselves are not accessible and should not be pursued.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles reasoning (who audits/aggregates credit behaviour) plus direct fetch

candidates.source_name: APEK – Asociace pro elektronickou komerci (e-commerce studies and press)
candidates.why_relevant: APEK represents roughly 75% of Czech online-retail turnover and describes 'platební řešení' as part of the ecosystem it covers. Its studies portal (data.apek.cz, plus a community studies area) and press pages are the demand-side counterpart to the provider press releases in this cell: they are where payment-method share at Czech checkouts, including deferred payment, is measured independently of any single BNPL vendor's marketing. Its member list also maps which payment providers court the merchant side.
candidates.access_status: partially open (some study content sits behind a member community area)
candidates.legal_status: public association publications; member-area content likely restricted
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly crawl of /novinky-apek and /pro-novinare plus data.apek.cz; treat komunita.apek.cz/s/apek-studie/ as likely gated and do not attempt authenticated access.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles reasoning (who reveals indirectly: the merchants' own association) plus direct fetch

candidates.source_name: CzechCrunch – fintech coverage
candidates.why_relevant: The leading Czech startup/tech outlet and the most reliable secondary channel for BNPL funding rounds, ownership changes and executive interviews that companies do not put in formal press releases — the kind of reporting that would, for example, be the natural place to find detail on Twisto's move under Param, or on Revolut's and other challengers' Czech consumer-credit ambitions. Useful as a corroboration and event-discovery layer rather than a primary disclosure source.
candidates.legal_status: copyrighted journalism — index and cite, do not republish
candidates.suggested_collection_method: RSS/tag-feed monitoring on fintech and company-name keywords (Twisto, Skip Pay, Home Credit, Essox, Cofidis, Zonky, PlatímPak, odložená platba, BNPL); store headline, URL, date and a short quote only.
candidates.discovered_via_method: actor-map reasoning about Czech tech/fintech media; direct fetch

candidates.source_name: International Personal Finance plc – investor relations (parent of Provident Financial CZ)
candidates.why_relevant: IPF is the LSE-listed parent of the Provident home-credit/consumer-lending business, which has a long-standing Czech operation, and IPF has historically reported a European home-credit segment with country-level detail. That makes it one of very few sources publishing audited, segmented Czech consumer-credit performance on a fixed reporting calendar. Not confirmed on this pass because the site returned a bot-challenge page.
candidates.access_status: bot-defended on this attempt; presumed live
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Retry with a browser-grade client (headless browser with realistic headers) or collect the same filings from the LSE/RNS feed instead of the corporate site. Also confirm whether the Czech Provident entity is still in the group perimeter before investing collection effort.
candidates.discovered_via_method: actor-map reasoning about foreign-listed parents of Czech consumer lenders; direct fetch attempt
candidates.observed_blocker: Fetch returned a page whose only content was the header 'Challenge Validation' — consistent with a WAF/bot-challenge interstitial rather than a dead endpoint.

candidates.source_name: ČSOB – Vztahy s investory (parent of Skip Pay)
candidates.why_relevant: Skip Pay's own site links to csob.cz as its parent. ČSOB's investor-relations area is the expected home of Czech annual reports and mandatory disclosures for the group that owns the leading bank-backed BNPL brand, and KBC Group's own IR carries the consolidated view. Any consolidated commentary on Skip Pay volumes or strategy would surface here rather than on skippay.cz. The Czech IR URL returned HTTP 500 on this attempt, so the exact path is unconfirmed.
candidates.access_status: server error on this attempt; presumed live
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Re-attempt from the csob.cz homepage navigation rather than a guessed portal path; in parallel collect the consolidated view from KBC Group IR, filtering for 'Skip Pay' and Czech consumer finance.
candidates.discovered_via_method: ownership snowball from skippay.cz, which links to csob.cz
candidates.observed_blocker: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error on https://www.csob.cz/portal/csob/vztahy-s-investory. Treated as an unverified path, not as a dead source.

negative_findings.description: The session's WebSearch budget was already fully consumed (200 of 200 calls) before this cell began, so not a single search-engine query could be executed. The mandated cs/en dual-language query sweep — including the supplied seed queries and the extensions prepared for them — was therefore never run.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero search-engine queries executed. All discovery was carried out by direct HTTP fetching of hypothesised URLs plus link-following (snowball) from fetched pages, with first-principles reasoning about who must publish, who benefits, who regulates and who aggregates used to generate the initial URL hypotheses. Czech-language coverage was still achieved, but through Czech-language site navigation and Czech terminology in URL construction rather than through Czech-language search queries.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Snowball-from-known-actors is systematically biased toward incumbents with good websites. It will under-discover small, new or low-web-presence providers, regional media, court and enforcement records, and any actor not linked from a page already visited. The cell's actor map should be regarded as strong on the majors and thin on the tail until a search sweep is run.

negative_findings.description: Cofidis CZ (COFIDIS a.s.) clearly maintains a news/press area — the homepage 'O nás' navigation lists novinky (news) alongside corporate responsibility and awards — but the actual URL could not be resolved.
negative_findings.result_summary: Four candidate paths were fetched and all returned HTTP 404: https://www.cofidis.cz/tiskove-zpravy, https://www.cofidis.cz/o-nas, https://www.cofidis.cz/o-nas.html and https://www.cofidis.cz/cs/o-nas/novinky.html. A sitemap fetch at https://www.cofidis.cz/sitemap.xml also returned HTTP 404.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cofidis is one of the named seed actors and ships two distinct Czech checkout products (iPlatba and Pay Na splátky), so its press channel is materially in scope. Leaving it unresolved is a real gap in the press-release layer for this cell.

negative_findings.description: Raiffeisenbank CZ's media centre could not be located, which matters because its PlatímPak BNPL brand publishes no press releases of its own — platimpak.cz/pro-media offers only a spokesperson contact, two logo versions and a brand manual PDF, and explicitly points readers to the bank's own media centre.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both https://www.rb.cz/o-nas/pro-media and https://www.rb.cz/o-nas/pro-media/tiskove-zpravy returned HTTP 404. The only confirmed rb.cz path found was the privacy page linked from platimpak.cz: https://www.rb.cz/informacni-servis/ochrana-osobnich-udaju, suggesting the site uses an /informacni-servis/ style hierarchy that was not further explored.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: PlatímPak is a bank-owned deferred-payment arm sitting squarely in this cell, and without the parent bank's press channel there is no release-level feed for it at all.

negative_findings.description: Zonky no longer operates as an independent publisher. Its site footer reads '© 2026 Air Bank a.s., člen skupiny PPF, poskytovatel služby Zonky', and its navigation contains no press, media, news or blog section at all — only o-zonky, kontakty, poradna, dokumenty, cenik and an affiliate programme.
negative_findings.result_summary: Confirmed absence of any press/media/news section on zonky.cz. Zonky-related disclosure has migrated upward to Air Bank (which does maintain /pro-novinare/ and /novinky/) and to PPF group reporting.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Zonky is a named seed actor. Any collection design that budgets for a standalone Zonky press feed will silently collect nothing; the routing to Air Bank and PPF must be made explicit in the collection plan.

negative_findings.description: None of the Czech-domiciled specialists in this cell publish annual reports or audited financial statements on their own websites. Home Credit a.s.'s /o-nas page carries a legal-entity identity (IČO 269 78 636, Brno, PPF group, ČNB-authorised as payment institution and non-bank consumer-credit provider) and a client ombudsman, but no reports; ESSOX, Twisto, Skip Pay and PlatímPak similarly expose only terms, pricing and press material.
negative_findings.result_summary: Confirmed across homecredit.cz, essox.cz, twisto.cz, skippay.cz and platimpak.cz: no výroční zpráva or účetní závěrka links found on any of them.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: It means the financial-statement layer for this entire cell depends on the Sbírka listin and on foreign parent disclosures (PPF, Home Credit Group, KBC/ČSOB, Inbank Group, Param). Collection design must treat the register as the primary financial source rather than as a fallback.

negative_findings.description: Two important register/statistics endpoints returned essentially no content to a plain HTTP fetch: https://dataor.justice.cz/ returned only the header 'Opendata', and https://www.cnb.cz/arad/ returned only 'ČNB ARAD'. The new unified register portal https://verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz/ rendered only partially.
negative_findings.result_summary: Content is almost certainly assembled client-side. This is a rendering hypothesis, not evidence that the services are unavailable — the ČNB and Ministry of Justice endpoints are official infrastructure and should be assumed live.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are exactly the machine-readable, licence-clean sources the collection layer should prefer over scraping corporate sites. Getting them working requires a headless browser or the documented data/API endpoints, and that work should be planned rather than discovered late.

negative_findings.description: No Czech trade association, self-regulatory body or code of conduct specific to BNPL or deferred payment was located. The nearest structures found were ČLFA (broad non-bank finance and consumer credit, which does include Twisto Payments a.s. as a member) and SOLUS (credit registries).
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched by navigation and by reasoning about who would organise such a body; found none. Czech BNPL providers appear to organise through the general non-bank finance association rather than a BNPL-specific one.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: There is no single BNPL-sector voice publishing volume or conduct data for Czechia, so sector aggregation must be assembled from ČLFA statistics, ČNB supervisory material and APEK e-commerce studies rather than from a dedicated body.

negative_findings.description: Two attempts to reach general search infrastructure and one foreign issuer site were repelled by bot defences.
negative_findings.result_summary: https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/ returned a CAPTCHA challenge page ('Please complete the following challenge...', error code 90d2) instead of results, closing off the workaround for the exhausted WebSearch budget. https://www.ipfin.co.uk/en/investors.html returned a page containing only 'Challenge Validation'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that search-engine-based discovery was genuinely unavailable on this pass, and flags IPF as needing a browser-grade fetcher or an RNS-feed route in the collection layer.

coverage_gaps.description: The mandatory bilingual search-engine sweep was not performed at all because the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before this cell started. Prepared but unexecuted Czech queries included: 'Twisto tisková zpráva odložená platba obchodníci výsledky'; 'Skip Pay ČSOB odložená platba tisková zpráva integrace'; 'nákup na splátky online platba později Česko tisková zpráva integrace'; 'poskytovatel spotřebitelských úvěrů Česká republika hospodářské výsledky výroční zpráva'; 'kup teď zaplať později Česko podíl na trhu'; 'PlatímPak Raiffeisenbank odložená platba e-shopy'. Prepared English queries included: 'Czech BNPL buy now pay later press release merchant integration results'; 'Home Credit Group annual report Czech Republic consumer finance'; 'Czech Republic deferred payment provider market share 2026'.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with search budget available, executing the query list above in both cs and en, and going past the first page of results. Treat the present candidate list as a verified seed set to be extended, not replaced.

coverage_gaps.description: The long tail of Czech consumer-credit providers was identified by name but not individually profiled: Zaplo Finance s.r.o. (ČLFA member), PROFI CREDIT Czech a.s., Creditstar Czech s.r.o., CreditPortal a.s., AvaFin Czech s.r.o., Simfina a.s. (all SOLUS members), plus Provident Financial CZ and Fair Credit. ČLFA states it has 14 licensed consumer-credit providers as members, so at least a handful remain unnamed here.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve the full ČNB JERRS list of nebankovní poskytovatelé spotřebitelského úvěru into a canonical actor table keyed by IČO, then profile each for a press channel and a Sbírka listin filing history. The JERRS web service makes this cheap and systematic.

coverage_gaps.description: Foreign BNPL entrants into the Czech market were not investigated. Klarna, PayPo and similar pan-European providers were neither confirmed nor ruled out as active in Czech checkouts. Notably, none of them appeared in the Shoptet payments addon catalogue, which is suggestive of limited Czech platform penetration but is not proof of absence.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check the addon catalogues of the other Czech e-shop platforms (Upgates, FastCentrik, Retailys, eBrana were all named by Skip Pay as integration targets) and the major gateways' method lists for foreign BNPL brands, then follow any hit back to the provider's Czech-language pages.

coverage_gaps.description: The 'wallet providers' half of the cell brief is materially under-covered. Twisto and Skip Pay were treated primarily as BNPL, and no dedicated pass was made on Czech wallet or stored-value propositions — Revolut CZ, Fidoo, Qerko and any bank-issued wallet arms were not examined, and the boundary against the card-acceptance cell was not tested.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated wallet sub-pass using Czech terms 'digitální peněženka', 'elektronická peněženka', 'platební karta v mobilu', 'předplacená karta', cross-referenced against the ČNB list of instituce elektronických peněz in JERRS, and agree an explicit boundary with the neighbouring cells.

coverage_gaps.description: Regulatory enforcement and supervisory output was not collected. ČNB sanction decisions, supervisory benchmark reports, the Zpráva o výkonu dohledu and the Zpráva o finanční stabilitě were all reasoned about as relevant categories but none were fetched; likewise, no court or arbitration records, no ombudsman (finanční arbitr) decisions, and no Česká obchodní inspekce consumer-protection actions.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a supervisory/enforcement sub-pass covering cnb.cz sanction lists and supervision reports, the Finanční arbitr's decision database, and ČOI. Enforcement documents are high-credibility, dated, and often the only public source of adverse detail about consumer-credit conduct.

coverage_gaps.description: Czech specialist personal-finance and retail-trade media were not fetched on this pass — Peníze.cz, Měšec.cz, Finparáda, Lupa.cz, e15, Hospodářské noviny, MediaGuru and retail titles are all plausible carriers of BNPL pricing comparisons and merchant-adoption reporting. Only CzechCrunch was reached.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch and classify each of the above, prioritising those that publish structured product comparisons (Finparáda, Měšec.cz) since those double as pricing datasets. Cashbot's /napsali-o-nas/ press-clipping page is a cheap way to discover which outlets actually cover this sector.

coverage_gaps.description: No specific ARAD dataset covering consumer credit or non-bank credit providers was identified, because the ARAD entry point returned an empty JS shell. The sector-level quantitative series that would let provider claims be benchmarked therefore remains unlocated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Access ARAD with a headless browser or via its documented data-export interface, identify the series codes for spotřebitelské úvěry (bank and non-bank), and register those codes in the collection plan alongside the ČLFA statistics.

brief: The Czech consumer-credit/BNPL/wallet cell splits cleanly into three publishing layers. The specialists — Twisto (now owned by Turkey's Param), ČSOB's Skip Pay, PPF's Home Credit a.s., KB/Société Générale's ESSOX, Cofidis CZ, and the previously unlisted bank-owned arms PlatímPak (Raiffeisenbank) and Inbank CZ — are prolific, dated press publishers with quantitative nuggets (Skip Pay's 99% on-time repayment claim, ESSOX's contract and unit volumes, Home Credit's May 2026 exit from short-term lending), but not one of them publishes financial statements on its own site. That financial layer therefore lives entirely in the Sbírka listin at justice.cz and in foreign parent disclosures (PPF, Home Credit Group, KBC/ČSOB, Inbank Group), while ČNB's JERRS register is the authoritative and machine-readable spine for licence status and for discovering the long tail of licensed providers. The richest and most differentiated finding is the merchant-integration layer that the cell rationale anticipated: the Shoptet addon catalogue enumerates the full competitive set of Czech checkout BNPL providers in one place, Skip Pay's developer portal names its gateway and SaaS-platform partners explicitly, Twisto's docs mark which integration paths are deprecated, and Twisto and PlatímPak both publish browsable partner e-shop directories that can be diffed into an adoption time series. The main caveat on this pass is methodological: the session's search budget was exhausted before the cell began, so everything here came from direct fetching and link-snowballing, which biases the map toward well-resourced incumbents and leaves the smaller lenders, foreign entrants and the wallet sub-sector thinly covered.
